notes: The refuter's question (named procedures or execution closure) is settled by the text: the restriction is printed twice, as §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR15/GR16 in the same rule list whose GR11 defines 'range' as the statements executed, including those reached by CALL, EXIT, GO TO and PERFORM, and its declarative carve-out ('whose execution is caused within that range') only has content over that range. So the rule restricts the EXECUTED range. A program whose executed range mixes segments (the refuter's r03, and by the letter CCVS-85 SG102A/SG103A) violates it, and its result is undefined (§1985:I.1.6): the 1985 text requires no diagnosis, so accepting and running r03 conforms, as does diagnosing a span the named procedures fall through (p03, r02, r05-r07); GnuCOBOL 3.2 diagnoses none of it. But the compiler's model is the PHYSICAL span procedure-name-1 THRU procedure-name-2, and that refuses conforming programs: when the named span contains a section of another segment that no execution of the range reaches, the executed range lies in one permitted set and COBOL6877 is still issued, where §1985:I.1.5.2.2 requires acceptance. Probes s1 (from 0: A 60 GO TO C 60 over B 10), s2 (from 5: A 10 / B 60 / C 10), s3 (from 70: A 70 / B 10 / C 70), s4 (from 70: A 10 / B 70 / C 10), s5 (from 5: A 60 / B 10 / C 60) are all refused; each executed range is A and C only. The named-procedure checks are right on every program whose span is executed (the reader's and refuter's probes). docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3.8 is wrong in its framing: it presents 'the procedures the statement NAMES' as the reading of 'range' and rejects the closure; the text makes the closure the rule, and the compiler's choice is which violations to diagnose (the named fall-through span; not nested PERFORM ranges, because CCVS SG102A/SG103A would be refused), and it must not refuse a section the range cannot reach. For this rule the witness of the over-refusal is s2 (from 5, executed range 10 only). kb/Work PB5442 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set6/decisions.json).
